Chapter 6: The Sign Above the Cross — A Message for All.
Sometimes, it’s the smallest details that end up carrying the most weight, isn’t it? On the day of the crucifixion, there was a sign nailed right above Jesus’s head. It simply read, “King of the Jews.”
To the soldiers and the crowd gathered there, it probably seemed like nothing more than a cruel joke—just another way to mock someone who looked powerless in that moment.
But if you’ve ever felt misunderstood, or had someone slap a label on you that never quite fit, then you know there’s more to that sign than meets the eye.
Picture someone who’s spent their whole life being defined by other people’s opinions. Maybe they’ve been boxed in by labels that never matched who they really are. That sign above the cross? It was supposed to shame Jesus. Yet, it turned into something so much bigger—a declaration that the world had no idea how to define.
Even the way the sign was written—displayed in multiple languages—sent a message that reached everyone, no matter their background or the words they spoke.
Think about it: most of us spend years trying to prove ourselves, rewriting the stories others have written about us. But the sign above the cross flips that struggle completely upside down. It tells us that our identity isn’t about the world’s judgments— it’s about something deeper, something greater.
Even in the middle of mockery, the truth can’t be silenced. That sign was meant to limit, but instead, it became an invitation—an open door for anyone who’s ever wondered, “Do I really belong here?”
There’s a quiet but powerful freedom in realizing that no label can ever define your worth. The cross stands there as a reminder that every single story matters, that every life is seen and deeply valued.
So, what’s the message in the sign above the cross—written for all to read? It’s that no one is left out. You’re invited to step beyond any label and discover an identity rooted in a love that has no limits.
